proposal.root_cause: Billing import validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, compares the raw AMI register value directly against 12-month m3 usage history with no unit scaling (E-12); firmware v4.2 meters (rollout June 2026) report reads in native register unit "0.1 m3" instead of "m3" (E-13), so BV-17 misflags valid high consumption as anomalous and rejects the read at import (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), forcing estimate substitution. This explains 1184 of 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills (95.5%, E-11/M-ESTIMATED-BV17-SHARE). The cause of the larger ACTUAL-read dispute segment (1785/3025, E-03) remains undiagnosed (VOB-U-FIRMWARE-DEFECT-UNIFIES-ACTU, VOB-U-GENUINE-ERROR-VS-SEASONAL/USAGE-INCRE still OPEN), so no single structural remedy yet covers the whole surge.

proposal.summary: Dispute tickets at Lakeside Water roughly doubled from ~600/month to ~1220+/month in Aug-Sep 2026 (E-05). The requester (SH-CS) asked for an AI agent to auto-answer tickets and auto-fix whatever causes wrong bills (CL-01), but that framing was rejected because it assumed a single fixable defect without evidence (H-AI-AGENT-FIX REJECTED, contradicted by E-03, E-11). Deterministic queries ruled out a tariff change (E-02, E-06, CL-02=false), CRM response-time backlog (E-04), AMI export failure (H-AMI-EXPORT-FAILURE rejected by E-03/E-11/E-15), and field-read staffing gaps (H-FIELD-READ-GAP rejected by E-03/E-11/E-15, despite SH-FIELD's claim CL-03/E-07). The dominant, well-evidenced mechanism found is billing-import rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01, no unit scaling, E-12) misreading firmware v4.2 meters' native 0.1 m3 register unit (E-13) as m3, causing REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION import rejections for 1184 of 1240 disputed ESTIMATED-read bills (E-11, E-14, E-15 - independently corroborated across mdms-export and billing-db). This explains the ESTIMATED-bill segment, but the larger ACTUAL-read dispute segment (1785 of 3025 total, E-03) remains unexplained. Given this, the release delivers only the dispute-response-template work (draft_dispute_response_templates:DA-TICKET), citing the diagnosed BV-17 mechanism, while diagnosis of the actual-read defect and the BV-17 fix itself remain out of scope.
key_points: Problem as defined (PD-1@v2): dispute surge (E-05) is dominantly driven, for the ESTIMATED-bill segment, by billing-import rule BV-17's unscaled high-consumption check (E-12) misflagging firmware v4.2 meters' 0.1 m3 register reads (E-13), causing 1184/1240 disputed ESTIMATED bills to be rejected at import (E-11, E-14, E-15); this superseded an earlier, invalidated problem definition (PD-1@v1) that assumed the ACTUAL-read majority (E-03) pointed to a billing-calculation defect.

Establishment method: authoritative read-only tool queries across billing-db, crm-tickets, route-log, mdms-export and billing-config (E-01 through E-15) were used to test and reject competing hypotheses - tariff change (E-02/E-06), CRM backlog (E-04), AMI export failure, field-read staffing gap (E-07/CL-03) - leaving BV-17/firmware mismatch as the SUPPORTED mechanism (H-BV17-UNIT-SCALING-DEFECT, H-IMPORT-RULE-CHANGE).

What was released: only draft_dispute_response_templates:DA-TICKET, the minimum useful scope in solution design SD-2, drafting CRM dispute-response content that cites the diagnosed BV-17/firmware mechanism (E-11, E-12, E-13).

Why this decision: DEFINE Gate returned CONDITIONAL_PASS with deferred items tracked as open Verification Obligations; release proceeds as RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION because the released scope (customer-facing templates) does not depend on resolving the still-open ACTUAL-read root cause and makes no automated bill writes, respecting the K-BILLWRITE authority constraint.

Diagnosis and analysis actions on billing rules and actual-read bills (diagnose_billing_calculation_defect:DA-RULES, analyze_disputed_actual_read_bills:DA-BILL) were excluded from release scope because they are blocked by open CRITICAL/HIGH Verification Obligations.

limitations_explained: Three Verification Obligations remain OPEN and outside release scope: whether the BV-17/firmware defect also explains ACTUAL-read disputes (VOB-U-FIRMWARE-DEFECT-UNIFIES-ACTU), and whether disputed ACTUAL-read bills are genuine errors versus a real usage/seasonal increase (VOB-U-GENUINE-ERROR-VS-SEASONAL, VOB-U-GENUINE-ERROR-VS-USAGE-INCRE).
The root cause of the 1785 ACTUAL-read disputes (E-03), the numeric majority of all disputed bills, is not resolved by this release.
